dump.name: gtfo-inspection/dumper/dump.cs
dump.note: Local read-only copy. dump.cs records the declaring type, the il2cpp RVA, the file offset, the vtable Slot of every virtual/override and the exact parameter list.

interop.note: The generated interop assemblies are Il2CppInterop runtime-invoke thunks: every body is `il2cpp_runtime_invoke(il2cpp_object_get_virtual_method(this, methodInfo), ...)`, so they carry the member set (type, virtual/override, Slot, parameter list, field offsets) but no game logic. Every call relationship below comes from the native image, not from the interop bodies.

method: Read-only static analysis. No assembly is loaded into the CLR, no game process is started, nothing is written to a profile or to the game directory.

A method body starts at its dump.cs file offset (RVA minus 0x1A00 in this image, confirmed on three sites whose target is known from the dump) and is bounded by the next distinct RVA the dump gives the same declaring type.
An edge is a literal E8/E9 rel32 call or jump at that site; indirect dispatch (vtable, delegate, register) is never reported as an edge.
A caller scan is a linear sweep of the whole image for E8 whose rel32 resolves to the target RVA, so the caller sets reported below are complete for literal calls and say nothing about indirect ones.

answer.question: Which native body is 'this melee swing hit this target', does it run once per target, what can be read there (attacker, target, limb, damage, charge), and can the host observe it for every player?
conclusion: The per-target melee hit entry is Gear.MeleeWeaponFirstPerson::DoAttackDamage(MeleeWeaponDamageData, System.Boolean), RVA 0x1343920. Its complete literal caller set is three sites — 0x133B4DF and 0x133B99B inside MWS_AttackHit::Update (the hit state's per-entry loop over HitsForDamage) and 0x133ED6E inside MWS_Push::Update (the shove, which enters the same body with isPush set) — so one call is one hit of one target, and a swing that connects with three targets enters the body three times.

The hit's own data is Gear.MeleeWeaponDamageData: damageGO (the target GameObject), damageComp (its IDamageable), hitPos/hitNormal and the damageDone flag. The damage the hit will deal is the weapon's own field m_damageToDeal (0x2B4), which SetNextDamageToDeal(eMeleeWeaponDamage dam, float scale) fixes for the hit; the charge is the weapon's own state, Gear.eMeleeWeaponState, whose set has exactly two plain hit members (AttackHitLeft/Right) and two charge-hit members (AttackChargeHitLeft/Right). MeleeWeaponFirstPerson.m_hitPacket (0x2A0) is an SNet_BroadcastAction<pMeleeHitPacketStruct>.

The same hit on a machine that is not the wielder's is Gear.MeleeWeaponThirdPerson::DoAttackDamage(GameObject, Vector3, Vector3, System.Single, System.Boolean), RVA 0x13B8810, whose complete literal caller set is PlayerBotActionMelee.UpdateStateStrike (sites 0x19C07C2 and 0x19C0A7A). Its damage arrives as its own argument and its target as its first argument; its charge flag has no equivalent member on the third-person weapon that this analysis can tie to the swing, so the port is left absent there.

A human client's swing is NOT replayed through any melee weapon body on the host. The hit broadcast reaches Gear.MeleeWeaponThirdPerson::IncomingMeleeHit(pMeleeHitPacketStruct) (RVA 0x13B8EA0), which has no literal caller — it is the broadcast delegate target — and whose body calls only FX_Manager.PlayEffect, FeedbackManager.Play and sound: the packet spawns decals and feedback and applies no damage. The third-person damage body's only callers are the bot action, so a client's swing is invisible to the host on the weapon side.

What the host does receive from a client's swing is the replicated damage: Gear.Dam_EnemyDamageBase::ReceiveMeleeDamage(pFullDamageData) (Slot 47, RVA 0x137FEB0) is the master-side melee packet receiver, and the packet (pFullDamageData) carries a packed pAgent source (TryGet(out Agent)), a packed UFloat16 damage, a byte limbID and a uint gearCategoryId. It does not carry the charge, and the damage is packed — its decode needs the scale the receiver's own body holds — so that path cannot fill this row's five ports without guessing two of them.

Consequence for the row: the five ports exist together only on the machine that performs the swing (first person for the local player, third person for a bot swing this machine runs). The observation half therefore publishes there with the adapter's existing host gate, and a client's swing needs a client-to-host observation sync before the host can run a row for it; that sync does not exist in this build (the network layer carries commands client-to-host and facts host-to-client).
consequences: One fact per target per swing: the hit entry is per target, so the author's 'each target of one swing fires once' falls out of the native shape instead of needing a tally.
The push (shove) is a different action: the first-person body is entered with isPush set for push damage, and the row skips that entry rather than reporting a shove as a swing hit.
The attacker is the weapon's own Owner rather than the machine that observed the hit, so a bot's swing names the bot's own player reference.
The limb is the target part's own m_limbID on the damage limb the hit resolved, which is the same value the enemy domain's own limb rows name.

evidence.name: DoAttackDamage

directCallers.signature: MWS_AttackHit::Update (the hit state's per-target call, site offset +0x5EF)
MWS_Push::Update (RVA 0x133E7C0): the same entry is reached for the shove with isPush set

evidence.reason: The complete literal caller set is the melee weapon's own states — two sites in the hit state, one in the push state — and nothing else: no ranged body, no network receiver and no damage base calls it. That is the swing's own per-target hit entry, and the push site is why the observation skips a hit entered with isPush set.

evidence.name: DoAttackDamage
evidence.reason: The damage arrives as the body's own float argument and the target as its GameObject argument; the only callers in the image are the bot melee action's strike state, so this body is the non-first-person swing this machine runs for somebody else.

evidence.name: IncomingMeleeHit

calls.signature: FX_Manager::PlayEffect(bool, FX_GroupName, Transform, Vector3, Quaternion, bool)

evidence.reason: No literal caller (it is the broadcast action's delegate target) and its body only plays effects, feedback and sound. The client's swing therefore produces no melee damage body on the host.

evidence.name: ReceiveMeleeDamage
evidence.reason: The master-side melee packet receiver. Its packet carries the attacker, the limb byte and the gear category, but its damage is a packed UFloat16 whose decode scale is the receiver body's own, and it carries no charge flag — so it cannot fill this row's five ports without inventing two of them.

evidence.name: AttackHitLeft/AttackHitRight/AttackChargeHitLeft/AttackChargeHitRight
evidence.reason: The set's own members: two plain hit states and two charge-hit states. The observation reads charged=true only for the two charge-hit members, charged=false only for the two plain ones, and leaves the port absent for every other member.

unverified.statement: That MeleeWeaponFirstPerson.CurrentStateName is one of the four hit members at the moment DoAttackDamage runs.
unverified.reason: The state is set by ChangeState from the attack states, and the hit body is reached from those same states; the exact ordering inside the swing was not decoded. The read is written so an unexpected state leaves the port absent rather than publishing a false value.
unverified.whatWouldSettleIt: A runtime trace of CurrentStateName in the hit entry while a light and a charged swing are performed.

unverified.statement: That a third-person swing's charge can be read from MeleeWeaponThirdPerson.IsCharging / IsDischarging at the moment of its damage body.
unverified.reason: Both are native properties of the third-person weapon, but what writes them (the class item sync for a remote player, or the bot's own state machine) was not traced, so no value is published from that path.
unverified.whatWouldSettleIt: A runtime trace of both properties across a bot's charged and uncharged strike.

unverified.statement: That a client's melee swing is unobservable on the host through any melee weapon body.
unverified.reason: Positive evidence only: the broadcast receiver applies no damage and the third-person damage body's literal callers are the bot action. An indirect dispatch this analysis cannot resolve would not appear.
unverified.whatWouldSettleIt: A host/client session with the weapon logging at info: one melee swing per player and a count of the melee-hit lines on the host.

unverified.statement: That a swing which connects with several targets enters the hit entry once per target in a live match.
unverified.reason: The per-entry loop is read from the call structure of the hit state; nothing here was executed.
unverified.whatWouldSettleIt: A runtime count of the melee-hit facts for one swing into a group of three enemies.

limits: No claim about runtime behaviour: nothing here was executed, and a literal call edge only proves that a call site exists in the shipped binary.
The caller sets are complete for literal E8/E9 calls and say nothing about virtual or delegate dispatch; the vtable observations in the sibling evidence files use a separate dispatch scan.
The body bound (next RVA of the same declaring type) is the dump's own ordering; a body il2cpp stored out of line can only be swept short, which under-reports and never invents an edge.
Field offsets are the interop's own and the packet offsets are the explicit layout the interop declares; neither was validated against a live process.
